claim: Bases is officially defined by Obsidian as a core plugin that lets you create database-like views of your notes, storing data in local Markdown files and their properties.
quote: Bases is a core plugin that lets you create database-like views of your notes. ... All the data in Obsidian Bases is stored in your local Markdown files and their properties.

claim: Obsidian launched Bases as a new core plugin in version 1.9, displaying dynamic views of notes as tables, cards, and lists, with 1.10 adding Bases APIs for custom view layouts.
quote: Recently we launched Obsidian 1.9 with Bases, a new core plugin that lets you display dynamic views of your notes as tables, cards, and now lists. ... Today, we're releasing Obsidian 1.10 beta with Bases APIs to help you create your own custom view layouts.

claim: Obsidian 1.9.0 Desktop became available in early access on May 21, 2025 with Bases as the headline feature for turning note collections into structured databases.
quote: Obsidian 1.9.0 (Desktop) became available in early access on May 21, 2025. The headline feature in the 1.9.0 update is a new core plugin called Bases, which lets you turn collections of notes into structured databases.

claim: The Bases file format and formula syntax were refined in 1.9.2 (June 5, 2025), adding file properties like file.path, file.links, and file.tags and object-oriented chainable functions.
quote: New file properties: `file.path`, `file.links` (a list of all internal links in this file), and `file.tags` ... Functions are now object-oriented. Instead of `contains(file.name, "Books")`, the formula would be `file.name.contains("Books")`.

claim: Unlike Dataview, Bases require no coding — they are created and edited entirely with a visual editor and are fast even on large vaults.
quote: Bases are incredibly powerful. They are fast to create, fast to update, and return results incredibly fast ... Bases don't require any coding. You can create and edit Bases entirely with a visual editor.

claim: A base is conceptually a table of notes selected by filters such as tag or folder, with two sequential filter layers (All views, then This view).
quote: A base has two sections for filters, one titled All views, the second one This view. These are applied sequentially: first the "All views" filter selects a subset of your notes, then the "This view" filter prunes this selection further.

claim: Community framing positions Bases as the biggest Obsidian update since Properties, replacing the role Dataview has played for power users.
quote: Obsidian's New Bases Feature is The Biggest Update Since Properties

claim: Bases is positioned as the official, first-party successor to the Dataview community plugin, which has stagnated.
quote: How to Migrate to Obsidian Bases from Dataview
